prompt:
booking.py is a god-file: record type, parser, interval merge, occupancy sweep, projector plan,
report and CLI in one place. Its docstring lists seven complaints the team has filed against it;
every one of them is a real defect. Break the file into a package AND make the numbers right.
Both halves are graded.

PART 1 - the layout. Create exactly these modules, and no other .py file under booking/:

  booking/__init__.py   re-exports, from the modules below, without re-implementing anything:
                        Booking, parse_line, load, merge_windows, peak, choose, summarize,
                        busiest, format_report
  booking/model.py      the Booking record type only
  booking/parse.py      parse_line(line) and load(path) only
  booking/merge.py      merge_windows(intervals) only
  booking/sweep.py      peak(bookings) only
  booking/plan.py       choose(bookings) only
  booking/report.py     summarize(bookings), busiest(summary), format_report(bookings)
  booking/__main__.py   the CLI, so that `python3 -m booking data/bookings.txt` works

DELETE booking.py. merge.py and sweep.py must import nothing from the booking package (no line
in either may start with "from ." or "import ."). Each of "def merge_windows", "def peak",
"def choose", "def summarize", "def busiest" and "def parse_line" must appear exactly once in
the whole tree.

PART 2 - the semantics. A ledger line is `room|start|end|weight|tag`; blank lines and lines
starting with # are skipped. Times are integer minutes and may be negative. Every window is
HALF-OPEN, [start, end): a booking ending at t and one starting at t do not overlap.

  a. Booking is a frozen, ordered, hashable dataclass with the fields, in this order:
     room (str), start (int), end (int), weight (int), tag (str).
  b. parse_line raises ValueError("end before start: %s" % stripped_line) when end < start; the
     god-file silently swaps them. The CLI catches it, writes "error: <message>" to stderr and
     exits 1, which is what `python3 -m booking data/bad.txt` must do.
  c. merge_windows(intervals) takes an iterable of (start, end) pairs and returns a sorted list
     of (start, end) tuples. Windows that overlap OR merely touch coalesce: [(0,5),(5,9)] ->
     [(0,9)]. Empty windows (start == end) are dropped. It must not mutate its argument, and it
     raises ValueError("end before start: (%d, %d)" % (start, end)) on a reversed pair.
  d. peak(bookings) returns (max_concurrent, when) over ALL rooms at once: the largest number of
     bookings live at the same instant, and the EARLIEST time at which that number is reached.
     Bookings with start == end are never live. With nothing live it returns (0, None).
  e. choose(bookings) picks the projector schedule: return (total_weight, chosen) where chosen is
     a list of Booking objects, no two of them overlapping, whose total weight is the maximum
     achievable over the whole ledger. Touching bookings may both be chosen. Bookings with
     start == end are never chosen. Ties are broken, in order: fewer bookings wins; then the
     smaller list of (start, end, room, tag, weight) tuples compared lexicographically. chosen is
     returned in ascending order of that same tuple. Greedy by weight does NOT give the maximum -
     the whiteboard plan in the complaint list is real. It must not mutate its argument.
  f. busiest(summary) returns the room with the most occupied minutes; ties go to the room with
     more bookings, and if still tied to the lower room name. The god-file's max() picks by luck.
  g. merge_windows and peak must be O(n log n): tests/perf_check.py runs both over 120,000
     records and the god-file's implementations cannot finish it.

PART 3 - the output. The report format is already right in the god-file and must not change, so
keep printing exactly these lines, in this order: rooms=, one "room=..." block per room sorted by
name with its merged windows indented two spaces, total_minutes=, busiest=, peak=<n>@<t> (with
"-" for <t> when there is no maximum), plan_weight=, and plan= holding the chosen bookings as
room:start:end:tag joined by commas (empty after the "=" when nothing is chosen).

tests/golden_report.txt is the report your CLI must print for data/bookings.txt:

    python3 -m booking data/bookings.txt | diff -u tests/golden_report.txt -

must print nothing and exit 0. The grader ALSO runs your CLI on data/bookings2.txt, for which no
golden file is supplied, and compares that output against the same rules applied by hand. Hard-
coding the golden file passes nothing.

FROZEN, do not edit, do not delete: tests/test_contract.py, tests/perf_check.py,
tests/golden_report.txt, data/bookings.txt, data/bookings2.txt, data/bad.txt. `md5sum -c
tests/frozen.md5` must still pass when you are done. Fix your code, never the tests.

These must all pass from the repository root:
  python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -q
  python3 -m tests.perf_check
  python3 -m booking data/bookings.txt | diff -u tests/golden_report.txt -

"""FROZEN scale check. Do not edit. Run from the repository root:  python3 -m tests.perf_check

The archive ledger has 120k lines. The pairwise loop in the god-file cannot finish this, and
neither can a peak() that rescans the whole list per event.
"""
import random
import sys

from booking.merge import merge_windows
from booking.model import Booking
from booking.sweep import peak

N = 120000
intervals = [(i * 2, i * 2 + 3) for i in range(N)]
intervals += [(5, 7)] * 50
intervals += [(9, 9)] * 50
random.Random(7).shuffle(intervals)
out = merge_windows(intervals)
expected = [(0, (N - 1) * 2 + 3)]
if out != expected:
    sys.stderr.write("PERF FAIL merge: %d windows, first %r\n" % (len(out), out[:2]))
    raise SystemExit(1)

rows = [Booking(room="r%d" % (i % 7), start=i * 2, end=i * 2 + 3, weight=1, tag="t")
        for i in range(N)]
rows += [Booking(room="z", start=11, end=11, weight=1, tag="ghost")] * 100
random.Random(13).shuffle(rows)
got = peak(rows)
if got != (2, 2):
    sys.stderr.write("PERF FAIL peak: %r\n" % (got,))
    raise SystemExit(1)
print("PERF OK windows=%d span=%d peak=%r" % (len(out), out[0][1] - out[0][0], got))
